explanation: The OAuth service supports OAuth2 grants for consumer-report sharing, Dashboard and other Plaid services. This does not replace client_id/secret and Item access-token authentication on most product endpoints, and is distinct from bank OAuth in Link.
Fresh vendor table distinguishes free no-approval mock Sandbox, limited auto-approved US/CA Trial for eligible new signups, and reviewed paid full Production.

Vendor API overview documents broad JSON-over-HTTPS endpoints; Accounts reference confirms keyed Item requests. REST is used as a broad HTTP-API label here, not a claim of strict REST architectural conformance.
Vendor Sandbox docs explicitly describe a local MCP for creating mock Items, firing test webhooks and searching docs; scope remains development rather than unrestricted production banking.
Conditional is appropriate: a toolkit can be prototyped now, but full production product/geography entitlements are separately gated. No authenticated API calls were performed.
Fresh vendor FAQ says OAuth2 is required and basic API-key authentication is not supported.
Current pricing FAQ lists Starter at no charge with up to five connections; demo-company testing is documented. The separate remote MCP plan gate is correctly retained.
Vendor HTTP-resource documentation demonstrates contacts/invoices and create/update operations with XML or JSON payloads, supporting a broad REST accounting surface.
Opened vendor FAQ confirms OAuth2/PKCE, official remote URL, demo-only Starter access, Core-or-above real organisations and Xero-operated infrastructure.
Build is supported for the documented demo/private development route. It must not be read as free remote-MCP access to real customer organisations; the record explicitly limits that path.
Opened API guide requires authenticated user credentials and a generated user access token plus a licensed identity and IAM role; this is the Enterprise product, not consumer notebook access.

The final record labels entry paid, but current vendor licensing docs offer a full-featured free-trial subscription and explicitly include trial users in IAM setup. Recommend trial, retaining Enterprise license assignment and Cloud admin/IAM prerequisites. Product and setup pages disagree on trial duration, so avoid an exact duration.

Opened Preview API documents creating, retrieving, listing, deleting and sharing Enterprise notebooks. The RPC reference additionally documents notebook services; scope is focused notebook operations.

No conclusive official NotebookLM account-data MCP was identified. Search results for a Google /mcp/notebook endpoint refer to Colab Enterprise runtime tools, which cannot establish NotebookLM MCP availability. Unknown should remain.
Conditional remains appropriate because Enterprise setup, assigned licenses, user IAM permissions and Preview status apply, even though the paid-only access classification should change to trial.
Opened vendor quickstart uses X-Api-Key with a user-scoped key; vendor API feature page separately confirms customer-installable OAuth applications.
Opened vendor FAQ explicitly includes API keys, webhooks and SDKs on Free and all other plans, with self-generation and no admin approval. Keys retain the creating user’s meeting permissions.

Opened quickstart demonstrates GET /external/v1/meetings, cursor pagination, filters and transcript retrieval, supporting a focused REST meeting-data API. OAuth apps have different transcript-fetch constraints.
Fresh vendor meeting-notetaker page supplies api.fathom.ai/mcp, sign-in setup, all-plan availability and existing meeting-permission limits. This is not the unrelated Fathom analytics product.
Free self-issued keys plus a documented meeting API support build. This is a documentation assessment; no account signup or credentialed live execution was attempted.
